inspections.locator: §1 Introduction — ML-KEM and its three parameter sets (ML-KEM-512, -768, -1024).
inspections.accessBasis: United States federal standard, freely published.
inspections.reuseBasis: US government work; bounded original summary with attribution.
inspections.supportedClaimScope: That a federal standard now specifies a key-encapsulation mechanism, ML-KEM, in three parameter sets, believed secure against an adversary possessing a quantum computer.
inspections.boundary: Specifies an algorithm and its parameters. It does not state when any organisation must migrate, that migration is complete anywhere, or that quantum attack is imminent. "Believed to be secure" is the standard’s own hedge and is not a proof.

inspections.sourceIdentity: NIST Special Publication 2000-01, ABC's of Conformity Assessment
inspections.locator: Definition paragraph quoting ISO/IEC 17000, and the following paragraph enumerating testing, inspection, certification and accreditation.
inspections.accessBasis: United States government publication, freely available.
inspections.reuseBasis: US government work; bounded original summary with attribution.
inspections.supportedClaimScope: That conformity assessment is the demonstration that specified requirements relating to a product, process, system, person or body are fulfilled, and that it includes testing, inspection, certification and the accreditation of the bodies performing those activities.
inspections.boundary: Describes the field. It does not accredit anyone, does not establish that any particular assessment is adequate, and does not substitute for the ISO/IEC 17000 text it quotes.

inspections.locator: Article 25(1) and 25(2) — legal effects of electronic signatures.
inspections.accessBasis: Official EU legal publication, freely accessible.
inspections.reuseBasis: EUR-Lex reuse policy permits reproduction with acknowledgement; summarised here.
inspections.supportedClaimScope: That an electronic signature may not be denied legal effect or admissibility solely for being electronic, and that a qualified electronic signature has the equivalent legal effect of a handwritten one.
inspections.boundary: Addresses signatures by natural and legal persons. It does not confer contracting capacity on an autonomous machine, does not establish that an agent may bind a principal, and must not be read as authorising machine-formed contracts.
